message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide you can copy into a terminal or paste into a script.  
It shows the exact `curl` call (or equivalent Python) needed to post a comment to **VirusTotal** for the IP `192.168.1.1`.

---

### 1️⃣ What’s required?

| Item | How to obtain |
|------|---------------|
| **API Key** | Your personal VT key (`ABC321`). In production replace it with `<YOUR_VT_APIKEY>` – never hard‑code real secrets in shared scripts. |
| **Endpoint** | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments` |
| **HTTP Method** | `POST` |
| **Headers** | `x-apikey`, `Content-Type: application/json` |
| **Body** | `{ "data": { "type":"comment","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"} }}` |

> ⚠️ *Note:* The body structure follows VT v3 spec where the top level object contains `"data"`.

---

### 2️⃣ One‑liner `curl`

```bash
curl --request POST \
     --url https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments \
     --header 'x-apikey: ABC321' \          # <-- put YOUR actual key here
     --header 'content-type: application/json' \
     --data '{"data":{"type":"comment","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"}}}'
```

If everything goes well you’ll receive something like:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "<generated-comment-id>",
    "type": "comment",
    ...
  }
}
```

---

### 3️⃣ Equivalent Python snippet (requests)

```python
import requests
import json

api_key   = "ABC321"                     # ← replace with your key
ip_addr   = "192.168.1.1"
endpoint  = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip_addr}/comments"

payload = {
    "data": {
        "type": "comment",
        "attributes": {
            "text": "Confirmed #malware"
        }
    }
}

headers = {
    "x-apikey": api_key,
    "accept": "application/json",
    "content-type": "application/json"
}

resp = requests.post(endpoint, headers=headers, data=json.dumps(payload))

print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.json())
```

---

#### Quick sanity checks before running

* Make sure the IP actually has a record in VT (otherwise you'll hit “not found”).
* Verify you have permission to write comments—some accounts may be read‑only.
* If you see a rate‑limit response (`429 Too Many Requests`) wait a bit before retrying.

That’s all! Once executed, the comment will appear next to the IP entry in the VirusTotal web UI.
